name.text: Shared: Remediate rounding at the five boundary

questiontext.text:
Round \[ {@number@} \] to the nearest {@place_name@}.

The digit immediately to the right of the rounding place is exactly 5.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We are rounding \[ {@number@} \] to the nearest {@place_name@}.

The next digit is exactly \(5\). Using the school half-up convention, a boundary digit of \(5\) means the rounding digit increases by \(1\).

Therefore, \[ \boxed{{@answer@}}. \]

misconception-remediation

Learners resolve exact halfway rounding cases where the decision digit is five.

Targets the belief that an exact boundary digit of five may be rounded downward.

Original STACK question. Numbas items NUMBAS-21514 and NUMBAS-169559 were used only as interaction references. No source wording or mathematical content is copied.

None.

Curriculum alignment is maintained outside the question source.

prtcorrect.text: Correct. At an exact \(5\) boundary, round upward.

prtincorrect.text: Focus on the digit immediately to the right of the rounding place.

node.description: Checks whether an exact five boundary was rounded downward.

truefeedback.text:
You rounded the boundary value downward.

When the next digit is exactly \(5\), the school half-up rule says to increase the rounding digit by \(1\).

So move to the next higher multiple of the requested place value.

node.description: Checks whether the learner retained the five without respecting place value.

truefeedback.text:
The digit \(5\) tells you which direction to round; it is not added directly to the answer.

Round to a multiple of the requested place value.

falsefeedback.text: At an exact \(5\) boundary, round to the next higher multiple.

qtest.description: Correct half-up boundary rounding receives full credit.
Rounding an exact five boundary downward receives zero credit.
Keeping the five without applying place value receives zero credit.
